A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 51-page versions of the same Adam-convergence paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the equations, table, diagram, and Appendices A–D. Pages 5–51 match in both extracted text and rendering.

before.justification: v4 reports theoretical convergence results and mathematical proofs, including throughout Appendices A–D. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees; no original empirical results are reported.

after.justification: v5 retains the same theoretical results and proof appendices, without adding experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains identical moment updates, adaptive learning rates, and parameter updates. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical training or evaluation datasets or task suites. The theoretical optimization setting is unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated baselines. Table 1 retains the same works in its comparison of theoretical assumptions and convergence guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Algorithm 1 and Section 2.4 retain the same initialization and parameter schedules for the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: No ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies are added or removed. The appendices retain the same supporting lemmas and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probabilistic statements concern unchanged mathematical convergence results.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains every comparison entry and complexity bound, and Theorems 3.1–3.3 retain the same convergence findings. No numerical or qualitative results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: Assumptions 2.1–2.3, Theorems 3.1–3.3, the Section 4 derivations, and all definitions, lemmas, and proofs in Appendices A–D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of non-asymptotic complexity and last-iterate almost sure and L1 convergence under assumptions aligned with SGD. Their scope and novelty claims do not change.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ABC inequality, explanations of the analytical framework, and Section 2.4's qualifications about parameter restrictions and coverage are retained without substantive revision.

D1.justification: The documented initialization, smoothing term, and hyperparameter schedules are identical. No implementation, hardware, training-time, or code/data access information is added or removed; the new author designation is administrative.

R1.justification: Sections 1.1 and 2.3, Table 1, and the references retain the same cited works and positioning relative to previous Adam and SGD convergence analyses.

P1.justification: v5 adds an asterisk to Xiao Li's name and the footnote 'Corresponding author,' and updates the arXiv version/date label. The substantive prose, terminology, headings, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new first-page footnote causes limited spacing changes and prose reflow across pages 1–4, including a slight vertical shift of Algorithm 1. Table 1 and the appendix dependency diagram retain their content and design; pages 5–51 render identically.

improvement.justification: v5 identifies the corresponding author and makes associated minor layout changes, but retains the same scientific content, explanations, and complete proof appendices. These administrative edits provide no meaningful net change in the paper's overall quality.
